10:59 -!- jal0_ZzZ is now known as jal0
11:02 < Filip> morning jal0
11:07 < jal0> morning filip: had to get some coffee
11:09 < jal0> got the find4173() function working... it couldnt find it. i did a general scan, and the HalGetBusData returned nothing on the bus. oh well, it was a good thought. besides msdn says that all of the halx functions are depreciated and should not be used.
11:11 < antagonizt> morningjal0... could be usefull for other projects (not directly)... you should put it out there...
11:12 < jal0> ok i'll set up a link on my page.
11:14 < Filip> so there is no 4173 inside the BE 
11:16 < jal0> not sure, the Halx function retured 0 for all pci addresses, which means either their is no devices on the pci bus or that the drivers do not support those functions.
11:16 < Filip> jal0, if you've got some spare time, could you also look at CF code ? maybe there is similar code to look for CF adapters
11:16 < jal0> ok
11:17 < Filip> jal0, did you read my questions/remarks in yesterday's log regarding  EE design ?
11:17 < jal0> ? not sure, what was it
11:17 < Filip> the silkscreen labels being grouped in 3 ranges
11:17 < Filip> starting at 1 for cpu etc
11:17 < Filip> >200 for power
11:18 < jal0> not sure what you mean/want to know
11:18 < Filip> >300 for touchpanel, earphone, ...
11:18 < Filip> well, you as an ee, how do you label your components ? by logical group of functions/devices ?
11:19 < Filip> why would the designed of the be start  numbring certain parts starting at 1, others at 200 and 300 ?
11:19 < jal0> usually just start at 1 and increment as you go, 
11:20 < Filip> and the numbering scheme is for almost all components: connectors, ics  , .... 
11:20 < jal0> no, never skip number
11:20 < Filip> could it be cpu and core stuff is in >0 , power >200 and i/o >300 ?
11:21 < Filip> like different teams worked on sub-systems independantly ? or re-used exsiting blocks ?
11:22 < jal0> usually the number indicates the train of though of the engineer. ie you start with the design of the power supply, so all the components related to the power supply will be sequentially grouped.
11:22 < Filip> hardware buttons are in >0 (same as cpu)
11:25 < Filip> so it might provide some hints on where to look for certain functions (like we know where video lives, other functions from the same group are more likely to use the same chip)
11:26 < jal0> sad to say, that in most cases, the engineer is not the one who does the actualy layout. usually layout is a department all to its own. the engineer will publish requirements that the layout guys must follow, other than that the numbering scheme is usually in no coherent order execept maybee that components sometime are sequentially groups around functional bounds
